question: The Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana is for Indian citizens in the age group of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 18 to 50 years.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) is a government-backed life insurance scheme available to people in the 18 to 50 years age bracket having a bank/post office account. (प्रधानमंत्री जीवन ज्योति बीमा योजना — 18 से 50 वर्ष)

 

• It was launched on 9 May 2015 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Kolkata, along with PMSBY and Atal Pension Yojana.

 

• It provides a life cover of ₹2 lakh in case of death of the insured, for any reason, on payment of a nominal annual premium (currently ₹436 per annum, revised from ₹330).

 

• The scheme is administered through Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) and other life insurers willing to offer it on similar terms, and is renewed annually.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) is a companion accident insurance scheme for the 18 to 70 years age group, offering a cover of ₹2 lakh for accidental death/full disability at ₹20 per annum.

 

• Atal Pension Yojana (APY) is a pension scheme for the unorganised sector, open to those aged 18 to 40 years.

 

NOTE

 

• 40 to 70 years / 29 to 55 years / 35 to 60 years (Options 1, 3, 4): None of these match the actual eligibility band of PMJJBY, which is 18 to 50 years.

question: Pandit Jasraj, Bhimsen Joshi and Zakir Hussain are associated with which form of music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hindustani Classical Music.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Jasraj, Pandit Bhimsen Joshi, and Ustad Zakir Hussain are all celebrated exponents of Hindustani Classical Music, the classical music tradition of North India. (हिंदुस्तानी शास्त्रीय संगीत — पंडित जसराज, भीमसेन जोशी, जाकिर हुसैन)

 

• Pandit Jasraj was a vocalist of the Mewati Gharana, known for his devotional and classical renditions.

 

• Pandit Bhimsen Joshi was a vocalist of the Kirana Gharana and a Bharat Ratna recipient (2008), renowned for khayal singing.

 

• Ustad Zakir Hussain is a globally renowned tabla player, son of tabla legend Ustad Alla Rakha, and a recipient of multiple Grammy Awards and the Padma Vibhushan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Carnatic Music is the classical music tradition of South India, with exponents such as M. S. Subbulakshmi, Semmangudi Srinivasa Iyer, and the Trinity of Carnatic music (Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, Syama Sastri).

 

• Gharanas of Hindustani vocal music include Gwalior, Kirana, Agra, Patiala, and Jaipur-Atrauli.

 

NOTE

 

• Jazz Music (Option 1): A genre that originated in the African-American communities of the United States, unrelated to these artists.

 

• Pop Music (Option 2): A globally popular contemporary music genre, not associated with these classical musicians.

 

• Carnatic Music (Option 4): The South Indian classical tradition; these three artists instead belong to the North Indian Hindustani tradition.

question: Lord Curzon declared the partition of ________ in 1905.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bengal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lord Curzon, the Viceroy of India, announced and implemented the Partition of Bengal in 1905, dividing the province into East Bengal and Assam and West Bengal. (बंगाल विभाजन — लॉर्ड कर्जन, 1905)

 

• The stated official reason was administrative convenience, as Bengal was too large to be governed efficiently by a single administration, but the real motive was to weaken the growing nationalist movement by dividing Hindus and Muslims along communal lines.

 

• The partition took effect on 16 October 1905 and triggered the Swadeshi Movement and widespread boycott of British goods.

 

• Due to intense public protest, the partition was annulled in 1911 during the Delhi Durbar, and Bengal was reunited, while the capital of British India was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Swadeshi Movement promoted indigenous industries and the boycott of British goods, and is considered a precursor to the mass movements of the freedom struggle.

 

• Lord Curzon also passed the Indian Universities Act (1904) and undertook the restoration of the Taj Mahal.

 

NOTE

 

• Central Provinces (Option 1): Not the province partitioned by Curzon in 1905.

 

• Punjab (Option 2): Punjab was partitioned in 1947 at Independence, not by Curzon in 1905.

 

• United Provinces (Option 3): Not the province involved in the 1905 partition.

question: Which of the following can be referred to in the estimation of poverty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Monthly Per Capita Expenditure.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In India, poverty is officially estimated using consumption-expenditure data, and Monthly Per Capita Expenditure (MPCE) is the key indicator used to fix the poverty line. (मासिक प्रति व्यक्ति व्यय — निर्धनता आकलन)

 

• Committees such as the Y.K. Alagh Committee, Lakdawala Committee, Tendulkar Committee (2009), and Rangarajan Committee (2014) have all used per-capita consumption expenditure data (drawn from NSSO household surveys) to estimate poverty lines and poverty ratios.

 

• The Tendulkar Committee shifted the basis from calorie intake to MPCE on food, health, education, and other essential items, while the Rangarajan Committee further refined the methodology.

 

• Households whose MPCE falls below the estimated poverty-line expenditure are classified as living below the poverty line (BPL).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Poverty-line data in India is drawn from the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) consumption expenditure surveys, now conducted under MoSPI.

 

• The Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) 2022-23, released in 2024, is a more recent basis being examined for updating poverty estimates.

 

NOTE

 

• Average Marginal Utility (Option 1): A microeconomic concept relating to the additional satisfaction from consuming one more unit of a good; not used to estimate poverty.

 

• Maximum Support Value (Option 2): Not a recognised term used in poverty estimation.

 

• Minimum Support Price (Option 3): The guaranteed price the government offers farmers for certain crops; related to agricultural policy, not poverty measurement.

question: Guru Shashadhar Acharya was awarded the Padma Shri in 2020 for his contribution to which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhau dance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guru Shashadhar Acharya, a fifth-generation exponent of Seraikella Chhau, was conferred the Padma Shri in 2020 for his contribution to Chhau dance. (छऊ नृत्य — गुरु शशधर आचार्य, सरायकेला)

 

• Chhau is a semi-classical Indian dance form combining martial arts, athletics, and folk traditions, performed mainly in the eastern Indian states of Odisha (Mayurbhanj), Jharkhand (Seraikella) and West Bengal (Purulia).

 

• Chhau was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

 

• The three regional styles of Chhau are Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand), Purulia Chhau (West Bengal), and Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha), the last performed without masks.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Madhu Mansuri Hasmukh, also from Jharkhand, was conferred the Padma Shri in the same 2020 list for folk music.

 

• Notable Chhau gurus include Guru Kedar Nath Sahoo (Mayurbhanj Chhau) and other torchbearers of the Seraikella and Purulia styles.

 

NOTE

 

• Odissi Chaiti Ghoda dance (Option 1): A traditional folk dance of Odisha performed during the Chaitra month, unrelated to Guru Shashadhar Acharya.

 

• Folk and Sufi singing (Option 2): Not his field of contribution.

 

• Kathak dance and training (Option 3): Kathak is a North Indian classical dance form, distinct from Chhau.

question: According to the Indian calendar, Vasanta Season falls in which months?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chaitra-Vaisakha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian National Calendar (Saka calendar) divides the year into six seasons (Ritus), and Vasanta (Spring) Ritu corresponds to the months of Chaitra and Vaisakha. (वसंत ऋतु — चैत्र-वैशाख)

 

• The Saka calendar was adopted as India's official civil calendar on 22 March 1957, with Chaitra 1 as the first day of the year (falling around 22 March, or 21 March in leap years).

 

• The six Ritus in order are: Vasanta (Chaitra-Vaisakha), Grishma (Jyaistha-Asadha), Varsha (Sravana-Bhadra), Sarad (Asvina-Kartika), Hemanta (Agrahayana-Pausa), and Sisira (Magha-Phalguna).

 

• Vasanta Ritu roughly corresponds to mid-March to mid-May in the Gregorian calendar and is traditionally regarded as the most pleasant of the six seasons.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Saka calendar has 12 months, with the first month (Chaitra) having 30/31 days, aligned so that its dates run largely parallel to the Gregorian calendar.

 

• Vasanta Panchami, a festival marking the onset of spring, is celebrated in the month of Magha, shortly before Vasanta Ritu formally begins.

 

NOTE

 

• Jyaistha-Asadha (Option 2): These months correspond to Grishma (Summer) Ritu, not Vasanta.

 

• Margashirsa-Pausa (Option 3): Margashirsa is not one of the twelve official Saka months in this sequence; Pausa falls under Hemanta Ritu.

 

• Sravana-Bhadra (Option 4): These months correspond to Varsha (Monsoon) Ritu, not Vasanta.

question: Which of the following was one of the first countries to use iron for the manufacture of weapons in as early as 1700 BCE?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Romania.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Among the given options, Romania (in the wider Carpathian-Balkan region of southeastern Europe) is recorded as one of the earliest places to use iron for manufacturing weapons, with evidence dating back to around 1700 BCE. (लोहे के हथियार — रोमानिया, 1700 ईसा पूर्व)

 

• This falls within the broader transition period from the Bronze Age to the Iron Age in Europe and the Near East, when iron smelting technology gradually began replacing bronze for tools and weapons.

 

• Widespread iron use across Europe and Asia became common only later, from roughly 1200 BCE onward, which is conventionally taken as the start of the Iron Age.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Hittites of Anatolia (modern Turkey) are also credited among the earliest civilisations to smelt and work iron, around the second millennium BCE.

 

• In the Indian subcontinent, evidence of early iron use is generally dated somewhat later, associated with sites of the Painted Grey Ware culture.

 

NOTE

 

• Morocco (Option 2): Not identified among the earliest users of iron for weapon manufacture at this early date.

 

• India (Option 3): India's early iron-working evidence is generally dated later than 1700 BCE.

 

• Bulgaria (Option 4): Not the country credited with this particular early instance of iron weapon manufacture.

question: Which plant is considered a noxious weed that has a chemical defence mechanism to protect it from predators?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calotropis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Calotropis (commonly known as Aak/Madar, milkweed) is regarded as a noxious weed that protects itself from herbivores through a chemical defence mechanism — it contains a milky latex rich in toxic cardiac glycosides (cardenolides). (आक/मदार — रासायनिक रक्षा तंत्र वाला विषैला खरपतवार)

 

• The latex is bitter and poisonous to most animals, deterring grazing, though a few specialist insects such as the monarch butterfly caterpillar (on related milkweed species) can tolerate and even sequester these toxins for their own defence.

 

• Despite being toxic, Calotropis has traditional medicinal uses in Ayurveda and is also used as a source of natural fibre.

 

• It is widely found growing wild across wastelands, roadsides, and dry regions of India as an aggressive coloniser, which is why it is classified as a noxious weed.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known toxin-bearing plants include Datura (tropane alkaloids) and Nerium (oleander) (cardiac glycosides), both used historically in traditional medicine and as poisons.

 

• Cardiac glycosides from Calotropis and related plants have also been studied for potential anti-cancer and pharmacological properties.

 

NOTE

 

• Chicory (Option 2): A leafy plant used as a coffee substitute and in salads; not primarily known for a toxic chemical defence.

 

• Black henbane (Option 3): Contains tropane alkaloids and is toxic, but it is not the plant referenced here as the specific noxious weed with this defence mechanism.

 

• Field bindweed (Option 4): An invasive climbing weed, but its defence is mainly through aggressive growth rather than a notable chemical toxin.

question: Who discovered that diborane reacts with aldehydes and ketones to produce dialkoxyboranes, which are hydrolysed by water to produce alcohols?
solution_text:
The correct answer is HC Brown.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Herbert Charles Brown (H.C. Brown) discovered that diborane reacts with aldehydes and ketones to form dialkoxyboranes, which on hydrolysis with water yield the corresponding alcohols. (डाइबोरेन अभिक्रिया — एच.सी. ब्राउन)

 

• This reactivity of boron hydrides was part of Brown's pioneering work on organoboron chemistry, including the discovery of the hydroboration reaction, where diborane adds across carbon-carbon double/triple bonds.

 

• For his extensive contributions to the development of boron- and hydroboration-based reagents in organic synthesis, H.C. Brown was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1979, jointly with Georg Wittig.

 

• Brown's work made diborane and related organoboranes versatile tools for reducing carbonyl compounds and for regioselective and stereoselective synthesis in organic chemistry.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The hydroboration-oxidation reaction, developed by Brown, converts alkenes into alcohols with anti-Markovnikov selectivity and is a cornerstone reaction taught in organic chemistry.

 

• Brown shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Georg Wittig, known for the Wittig reaction.

 

NOTE

 

• Hugo Rudolph Kruyt (Option 2): A Dutch chemist known for his work in colloid chemistry, not diborane chemistry.

 

• Arthur Stoll (Option 3): A Swiss chemist known for phytochemistry and pharmaceutical research (notably at Sandoz), unrelated to this discovery.

 

• Arne Tiselius (Option 4): A Swedish biochemist known for developing electrophoresis techniques, unrelated to diborane chemistry.

question: Singhraj Adhana is associated with which of the following sports events?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shooting.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Singhraj Adhana is an Indian Paralympic shooter who competes in pistol shooting events. (सिंहराज अढाना — निशानेबाजी)

 

• At the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, he won a silver medal in the mixed 50m pistol SH1 event and a bronze medal in the mixed 10m air pistol SH1 event, becoming one of the few Indian Paralympians to win two medals at a single Games.

 

• He has also won medals at the Asian Para Games and various World Shooting Para Sport championships.

 

• He was honoured with the Arjuna Award for his achievements in para-shooting.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other prominent Indian para-shooters include Avani Lekhara (gold medallist, Tokyo and Paris Paralympics) and Manish Narwal (gold medallist, Tokyo Paralympics).

 

• India's contingent at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics won a then-record 19 medals, including 5 golds.

 

NOTE

 

• Badminton (Option 1): Not Singhraj Adhana's sport; notable Indian para-badminton players include Pramod Bhagat.

 

• High jump (Option 2): Not his event; associated instead with athletes like Nishad Kumar.

 

• Discus throw (Option 4): Not his event; associated instead with athletes like Vinod Kumar.

question: The origin of 'Carnatic music' is related to which of the following Dynasties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vijayanagar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The origin and systematisation of Carnatic music, the classical music tradition of South India, is traditionally traced to the Vijayanagara Empire. (कर्नाटक संगीत — विजयनगर साम्राज्य)

 

• Music theorists and composers under Vijayanagara patronage, most notably Purandara Dasa (regarded as the "Pitamaha" or father of Carnatic music), laid down the pedagogical framework (swaravalis, alankaras, geethams) still used to teach Carnatic music today.

 

• The Vijayanagara rulers, especially Krishnadevaraya, were great patrons of art, literature, and music, fostering a golden age of cultural development in South India.

 

• Carnatic music later flourished further under the patronage of the Thanjavur Nayaks and Marathas, culminating in the works of the Carnatic Trinity — Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, and Syama Sastri, in the 18th-19th centuries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Purandara Dasa (1484-1564) composed thousands of devotional songs (Kirtanas) in Kannada and is credited with devising the raga Mayamalavagowla as the foundational teaching scale.

 

• The Vijayanagara Empire (1336-1646) was founded by Harihara and Bukka and served as a bulwark of South Indian culture and Hindu political power.

 

NOTE

 

• Bahamani (Option 1): A Deccan Sultanate contemporary with Vijayanagara, primarily associated with Indo-Islamic architecture and culture, not the origin of Carnatic music.

 

• Chola (Option 2): Known for Tamil literature, bronze sculpture, and temple architecture (e.g., Brihadeeswarar Temple), predating the systematisation of Carnatic music.

 

• Pandaya (Option 3): The Pandya dynasty is known for Madurai's temples and early Sangam-age Tamil literary patronage, not the codification of Carnatic music.

question: Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar and Mahadev Govind Ranade carried out their work of religious reforms in Maharashtra through which of the following organisations?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prarthana Samaj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar and Mahadev Govind Ranade carried out their religious and social reform work in Maharashtra through the Prarthana Samaj. (प्रार्थना समाज — भंडारकर एवं रानाडे)

 

• The Prarthana Samaj was founded in Bombay in 1867 by Atmaram Pandurang, and it was later strengthened and expanded by leaders like M.G. Ranade, R.G. Bhandarkar, and N.G. Chandavarkar.

 

• It was inspired by the ideals of the Brahmo Samaj and focused on monotheism, the abolition of caste distinctions, and social reforms such as widow remarriage and the upliftment of women, working within the framework of Hinduism rather than seeking a complete break from it.

 

• M.G. Ranade was also a founding figure of the Widow Remarriage Association and the Indian National Congress, and a prominent judge and economist.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• R.G. Bhandarkar was also a renowned Sanskrit scholar and Orientalist, after whom the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (Pune) is named.

 

• Other affiliated reform bodies of the period in Maharashtra included the Widow Marriage Association (1861) and the Deccan Education Society.

 

NOTE

 

• Atmiya Sabha (Option 2): Founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in Calcutta (1815), a precursor to the Brahmo Samaj, not connected to Bhandarkar and Ranade's Maharashtra work.

 

• Theosophical Society (Option 3): Founded by Madame Blavatsky and Henry Olcott in New York (1875), later headquartered at Adyar, Madras — a separate organisation.

 

• Brahmo Samaj (Option 4): Founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in Bengal (1828); the Prarthana Samaj was its Maharashtra-based counterpart, but the two are distinct organisations.

question: Shri Omprakash Mitharval was in news for being conferred with Arjuna Award 2022 for his outstanding contribution in which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shooting.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Omprakash Mitharwal is an Indian para-shooter who was conferred the Arjuna Award in 2022 for his outstanding contribution to shooting. (ओमप्रकाश मिथरवाल — निशानेबाजी, अर्जुन पुरस्कार 2022)

 

• He competes in pistol shooting events in the para-sport category and has represented India at major international competitions, including World Championships and Asian Para Games.

 

• The Arjuna Award is conferred by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India, for consistently outstanding performance in sports over a period of four years.

 

• The 2022 Arjuna Award list included several other para-athletes and shooters recognised for their achievements in international competitions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The National Sports Awards in India also include the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award (highest honour), the Dronacharya Award (for coaches), and the Arjuna Award (for players).

 

• Other notable Indian para-shooters honoured in recent years include Avani Lekhara (Khel Ratna) and Singhraj Adhana (Arjuna/Padma Shri).

 

NOTE

 

• Wushu (Option 1): Not his sport; a Chinese martial art with Indian competitors like Narender Grewal.

 

• Table Tennis (Option 2): Not his sport; notable Indian paddlers include Bhavinaben Patel in para table tennis.

 

• Weightlifting (Option 4): Not his sport.

question: In which of the following years did India celebrate its 73rd Republic Day?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2022.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's first Republic Day was celebrated on 26 January 1950, the day the Constitution of India came into force. Counting inclusively, 26 January 2022 marked the 73rd Republic Day. (73वां गणतंत्र दिवस — 26 जनवरी 2022)

 

• Republic Day commemorates the adoption of the Constitution of India, which was passed by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949 (celebrated as Constitution Day/Samvidhan Divas) and came into effect on 26 January 1950.

 

• The date 26 January was chosen to honour the Purna Swaraj (complete independence) declaration made by the Indian National Congress on 26 January 1930.

 

• The main Republic Day parade is held at Kartavya Path (formerly Rajpath) in New Delhi, showcasing India's cultural diversity and military strength, with a foreign head of state typically as chief guest.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India celebrates three major national days: Republic Day (26 January), Independence Day (15 August), and Gandhi Jayanti (2 October).

 

• The Beating Retreat ceremony is held on 29 January, formally marking the end of the Republic Day celebrations.

 

NOTE

 

• 2019 (Option 2): This year corresponded to the 70th Republic Day.

 

• 2021 (Option 3): This year corresponded to the 72nd Republic Day.

 

• 2020 (Option 4): This year corresponded to the 71st Republic Day.

question: In which of the following states is the National Sports University located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Sports University (NSU), India's first sports university of national importance, is located in Imphal, Manipur. (राष्ट्रीय खेल विश्वविद्यालय — इंफाल, मणिपुर)

 

• It was established through the National Sports University Act, 2018, passed by the Parliament of India, under the aegis of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

 

• Manipur was chosen as the location partly in recognition of the state's rich sporting talent and its contribution of numerous national and international-level athletes, particularly in disciplines like boxing and weightlifting.

 

• The university aims to promote sports education, sports science, sports technology, and coaching at a national level.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Manipur is also home to prominent sportspersons such as Mary Kom (boxing) and Mirabai Chanu (weightlifting).

 

• Other notable national-level sports institutions in India include the Sports Authority of India (SAI), headquartered in New Delhi, and the Netaji Subhas National Institute of Sports (NSNIS) in Patiala, Punjab.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab (Option 2): Home to NSNIS Patiala, but not the National Sports University.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): Not the location of the National Sports University.

 

• Assam (Option 4): Not the location of the National Sports University.

question: What is the correct sequence of layers of Earth from the outside of the planet to the inside?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Crust (outermost) - mantle - core (innermost).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Earth is structured in three main concentric layers, from the surface inward: the Crust (outermost), the Mantle (middle), and the Core (innermost). (पृथ्वी की संरचना — भूपर्पटी, मैंटल, क्रोड)

 

• The Crust is the thin, solid outermost layer on which we live, comprising continental crust (mostly granitic, thicker) and oceanic crust (mostly basaltic, thinner).

 

• The Mantle lies beneath the crust and extends to a depth of about 2,900 km; it is largely solid but capable of slow plastic flow (convection), and is divided into the upper mantle (including the asthenosphere) and lower mantle.

 

• The Core, the innermost layer, is further divided into a liquid outer core (composed mainly of molten iron and nickel) and a solid inner core, extending to the Earth's centre at about 6,371 km depth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Mohorovicic Discontinuity (Moho) marks the boundary between the crust and the mantle.

 

• The Earth's magnetic field is generated by convective movements of molten iron in the liquid outer core, a phenomenon known as the geodynamo.

 

NOTE

 

• Mantle (outermost) - core - crust (innermost) (Option 1): Incorrectly places the mantle outermost and the crust innermost.

 

• Crust (outermost) - core - mantle (innermost) (Option 2): Incorrectly swaps the positions of the mantle and the core.

 

• Core (outermost) - mantle - crust (innermost) (Option 4): Reverses the entire correct sequence.

question: Which of the following dances is NOT predominantly performed in the Indian state of Odisha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhavai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bhavai is a folk dance predominantly performed in Rajasthan and Gujarat, not Odisha, making it the odd one out among the given options. (भवाई नृत्य — राजस्थान/गुजरात, ओडिशा नहीं)

 

• Paika is a traditional martial dance of Odisha performed by the Paikas (traditional foot soldiers), involving vigorous movements with swords and shields.

 

• Ghumra is a popular folk dance of Odisha, especially of the Kalahandi region, performed with a drum called 'ghumra' slung around the performer's neck.

 

• Dhap is a folk dance of Odisha named after the 'dhap' drum used to accompany it, commonly performed during festive occasions in western Odisha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Odissi is the principal classical dance form of Odisha, distinct from these folk dance forms.

 

• Bhavai dancers in Rajasthan and Gujarat are known for their skill in balancing multiple pots or items on their heads while dancing on a brass plate or the edge of a sword.

 

NOTE

 

• Paika (Option 1): A genuine folk/martial dance of Odisha, hence incorrect as an answer to "NOT performed in Odisha".

 

• Ghumra (Option 2): A genuine folk dance of Odisha, hence incorrect as an answer.

 

• Dhap (Option 3): A genuine folk dance of Odisha, hence incorrect as an answer.

question: The minimum requirement of microfinance loans for NBFC-MFIs is ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 75% of the total assets.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the RBI's Regulatory Framework for Microfinance Loans Directions, 2022, the minimum requirement of microfinance loans for NBFC-MFIs (Non-Banking Financial Company - Micro Finance Institutions) is 75% of the total assets. (एनबीएफसी-एमएफआई — कुल परिसंपत्तियों का 75%)

 

• This 2022 framework harmonised the definition of a "qualifying asset" for NBFC-MFIs with the new, broader definition of "microfinance loans" (collateral-free loans to low-income households), replacing the earlier, more restrictive criteria.

 

• Previously, under the older 2011-2015 framework, NBFC-MFIs were required to maintain not less than 85% (later revised to lower thresholds) of their net assets as qualifying assets; the 2022 directions standardised this at 75% of total assets.

 

• The remaining 25% of assets may be held in other permissible forms, giving NBFC-MFIs greater flexibility while still ensuring their primary business remains microfinance lending.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The RBI (Regulatory Framework for Microfinance Loans) Directions, 2022 introduced income-based eligibility (households with annual income up to ₹3,00,000) and removed the earlier interest-rate margin cap for NBFC-MFIs, replacing it with a board-approved policy.

 

• NBFC-MFIs are regulated by the Reserve Bank of India and play a significant role in extending small, collateral-free credit to low-income and rural households.

 

NOTE

 

• 75% of the total equity (Option 2): Incorrect base — the requirement is expressed as a percentage of total assets, not equity.

 

• 90% of the total assets (Option 3): Not the figure prescribed under the current RBI framework.

 

• 80% of the total equity (Option 4): Incorrect both in the percentage figure and the base used.

question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding removal of the President of India?

A. The impeachment process can be initiated in either House of Parliament.

B. The impeachment charges must be signed by the one-third members of the House in which the process is initiated.

C. In the impeachment process, a 30 days' notice should be given to the President.

D. The impeachment resolution is passed by a majority of two-thirds of the total membership of that House.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A and D only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 61 of the Constitution of India, the impeachment process of the President can be initiated in either House of Parliament, so Statement A is correct. (राष्ट्रपति पर महाभियोग — अनुच्छेद 61)

 

• Statement B is incorrect: The charge (resolution) must be signed by at least one-fourth of the total membership of the House in which it is moved, not one-third.

 

• Statement C is incorrect: The President must be given 14 days' written notice before the resolution is moved, not 30 days.

 

• Statement D is correct: After investigation, the resolution to remove the President must be passed by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the total membership of that House; the same procedure is then required in the other House as well before removal takes effect.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The impeachment of the President in India is a quasi-judicial process, and till date no President has ever been impeached.

 

• The grounds for impeachment under Article 61 are limited to "violation of the Constitution".

 

NOTE

 

• B and C only (Option 1): Both statements B and C are factually incorrect (one-fourth, not one-third; 14 days, not 30 days), so this combination is wrong.

 

• A, B and C only (Option 2): Includes the incorrect statements B and C while omitting the correct statement D.

 

• A, B, C and D (Option 3): Incorrectly includes statements B and C, which contain factual errors.

question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Right mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right to vote.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Right to vote is NOT a Fundamental Right under the Indian Constitution; it is a constitutional/legal right, granted under Article 326 (which provides for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies on the basis of adult suffrage) and further detailed in the Representation of the People Act, 1951. (मताधिकार — मौलिक अधिकार नहीं, संवैधानिक अधिकार)

 

• The Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III (Articles 12-35) of the Constitution and include six categories: Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.

 

• Right to Equality (Articles 14-18) and Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28) are both explicitly listed as Fundamental Rights.

 

• Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22) includes freedoms such as speech and expression, assembly, movement, and protection of life and personal liberty, and is also a Fundamental Right.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Right to Property, originally a Fundamental Right (Article 31), was removed by the 44th Constitutional Amendment (1978) and is now only a legal right under Article 300-A.

 

• The Right to Education (Article 21-A) was added as a Fundamental Right by the 86th Amendment (2002).

 

NOTE

 

• Right to equality (Option 2): A genuine Fundamental Right under Articles 14-18, so incorrect as an answer.

 

• Right to freedom of religion (Option 3): A genuine Fundamental Right under Articles 25-28, so incorrect as an answer.

 

• Right to freedom (Option 4): A genuine Fundamental Right under Articles 19-22, so incorrect as an answer.

question: When was the Smart Cities Mission launched in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2015.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Smart Cities Mission was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 25 June 2015. (स्मार्ट सिटी मिशन — 25 जून 2015)

 

• It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, aimed at promoting cities that provide core infrastructure, a clean and sustainable environment, and a decent quality of life through smart solutions.

 

• Initially, 100 cities were selected in phases through a "City Challenge" competitive process for implementation under the mission.

 

• The mission was launched alongside two related urban initiatives: the Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) and the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Key components of the Smart Cities Mission include Integrated Command and Control Centres (ICCCs), smart mobility, e-governance, and sustainable urban environment measures.

 

• The mission's implementation was originally intended to run through 2019-2020 and was subsequently extended in phases.

 

NOTE

 

• 2017 (Option 1): Not the launch year of the Smart Cities Mission.

 

• 2016 (Option 2): Not the launch year of the Smart Cities Mission.

 

• 2014 (Option 4): Not the launch year; 2014 saw the launch of other schemes such as Swachh Bharat Mission, not Smart Cities Mission.

question: What is the common term for Ancylostoma?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hookworm.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ancylostoma is the scientific genus name for the parasitic worm commonly known as the Hookworm. (एंकिलोस्टोमा — हुकवर्म)

 

• Species such as Ancylostoma duodenale and Necator americanus infect the human small intestine, attaching to the intestinal wall using hook-like mouthparts to feed on blood, often causing anaemia and malnutrition in infected individuals.

 

• Hookworm larvae typically enter the human body by penetrating the skin (commonly through bare feet in contaminated soil), migrate through the bloodstream to the lungs, and are then swallowed to reach the intestine.

 

• Hookworm infection is a significant public health concern in tropical and subtropical regions, including parts of India, due to poor sanitation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tapeworm infections in humans are commonly caused by genera such as Taenia (from undercooked pork/beef).

 

• Filariasis is caused by thread-like filarial worms such as Wuchereria bancrofti, transmitted by mosquitoes, and can lead to elephantiasis.

 

NOTE

 

• Tape worm (Option 1): The common name for cestodes like Taenia, not Ancylostoma.

 

• Round worm (Option 2): The common name generally used for Ascaris lumbricoides, a different intestinal parasite.

 

• Filaria worm (Option 3): Refers to filarial nematodes like Wuchereria bancrofti, not Ancylostoma.

question: 1,3-Dimethylbenzene is also known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is m-Xylene.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 1,3-Dimethylbenzene is the IUPAC name for m-Xylene (meta-Xylene), an aromatic hydrocarbon in which two methyl groups are attached to the benzene ring at the 1 and 3 (meta) positions. (1,3-डाइमिथाइलबेंजीन — मेटा-जाइलीन)

 

• Xylene exists in three isomeric forms based on the relative positions of the two methyl groups on the benzene ring: ortho-xylene (1,2-dimethylbenzene), meta-xylene (1,3-dimethylbenzene), and para-xylene (1,4-dimethylbenzene).

 

• Xylenes are widely used as industrial solvents and as raw materials in the production of polyester fibres and plastics (para-xylene, in particular, is a key feedstock for PET/terephthalic acid production).

 

• Xylene is derived from petroleum through catalytic reforming and is a common component of gasoline and industrial solvent mixtures.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Toluene (methylbenzene) has only a single methyl group attached to the benzene ring, unlike xylene's two.

 

• Para-xylene is oxidised to produce terephthalic acid, a key raw material for manufacturing polyester (PET).

 

NOTE

 

• BHC (Option 1): Benzene hexachloride, an organochlorine insecticide, structurally unrelated to dimethylbenzene.

 

• toluene (Option 3): Methylbenzene (C6H5CH3), which has only one methyl substituent, not two.

 

• terelene (Option 4): A trade name associated with polyester fibre (terylene), not a name for dimethylbenzene.

question: Who is known as the father of the green revolution in the world?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Norman Borlaug.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. Norman Ernest Borlaug, an American agronomist, is known as the "Father of the Green Revolution" in the world. (हरित क्रांति के जनक — नॉर्मन बोरलॉग)

 

• He developed high-yielding, disease-resistant semi-dwarf wheat varieties, which dramatically increased wheat production and helped avert famine in countries such as Mexico, India, and Pakistan from the 1940s to 1960s.

 

• For his contributions to global food security, he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.

 

• In India, Dr. M.S. Swaminathan is credited as the "Father of the Green Revolution in India" for adapting and popularising Borlaug's high-yielding wheat varieties within the Indian context.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dr. M.S. Swaminathan also chaired the National Commission on Farmers, whose recommendations shaped India's Minimum Support Price policy debates.

 

• The Green Revolution in India primarily transformed agriculture in states such as Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh from the mid-1960s onward.

 

NOTE

 

• Ralph Bunche (Option 1): An American diplomat and the first person of colour to win the Nobel Peace Prize (1950), for mediation in the Arab-Israeli conflict, unrelated to agriculture.

 

• Linus Pauling (Option 2): An American chemist, double Nobel laureate (Chemistry, 1954; Peace, 1962), known for work on chemical bonding, not agriculture.

 

• MS Swaminathan (Option 3): Known as the Father of the Green Revolution in India specifically, not globally; the question asks about the world.

question: The State of Kerala Vs Leesamma Joseph case deals with ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is persons with disabilities.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• State of Kerala & Ors. v. Leesamma Joseph (2021) is a landmark Supreme Court of India judgment dealing with the rights of persons with disabilities, specifically reservation in promotions. (केरल राज्य बनाम लीसम्मा जोसेफ — दिव्यांगजन आरक्षण)

 

• The Supreme Court held that persons with disabilities are entitled to reservation in promotions, not merely in initial recruitment, interpreting the Persons with Disabilities Act, 1995 (and its successor, the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016) purposively to ensure meaningful inclusion.

 

• The Court directed the State of Kerala to identify posts for reservation for persons with disabilities and to provide consequential reservation in promotion within a stipulated time frame.

 

• The judgment reinforced the principle that reservation benefits for persons with disabilities must extend across the career progression of an employee, not just at the entry level.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 replaced the earlier 1995 Act and expanded the categories of disabilities recognised in India from 7 to 21.

 

• Other significant Supreme Court rulings on disability rights include those interpreting reasonable accommodation and accessibility obligations of the State.

 

NOTE

 

• dowry (Option 1): Not the subject matter of this case; dowry-related jurisprudence involves cases under the Dowry Prohibition Act and Section 498-A IPC.

 

• the economic weaker section (Option 2): Not the subject of this case; EWS reservation was addressed in cases like Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India.

 

• education (Option 3): Not the subject matter of this particular case, which concerns employment/promotion rights.
